title: Your First Weekend at Drew University, Shared as Cards
description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack in The Forest
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned residence hall during your morning time slot to begin your transition into the Drew community.
cards.short_summary: The official start of the fall semester for new first-year and transfer students.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Move-in for Fall 2026 takes place on the morning of Friday, August 28, with assigned times based on housing.
cards.source_title: Experience Fall Orientation at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Required for all new residential students; check your Drew email for specific building assignments.

cards.title: Formal Welcome to Campus
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Tradition
cards.notes: Join faculty and staff for this formal induction ceremony that marks the official start of your academic journey.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial welcome for new students and their families held on move-in Friday.
cards.evidence_claim: The Opening of School Ceremony is held on the afternoon of August 28, 2026, where faculty and staff formally welcome the community.
cards.source_title: Experience Fall Orientation at Drew University
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and their families; typically held in a central campus location.

cards.title: Grab a Bite at the EC
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Social
cards.notes: Visit the campus hub for dinner and explore the 1867 Lounge or the various food options like pizza and pasta.
cards.short_summary: The central student union and gathering place located between residences and academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ehinger Center (EC) serves as a gathering place with dining options including pizza, pasta, and a Starbucks.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; dining hours vary by station. Student ID required for meal plans.

cards.title: Friday Night Fun
cards.subtitle: Late Night Programming
cards.notes: Head back to the EC for late-night activities designed to help you meet fellow students in a relaxed environment.
cards.short_summary: Weekly late-night social events hosted by the Office of Student Activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Drew Night Life plans late night events every Friday night starting at 8pm in the Ehinger Center.
cards.access_notes: Events typically begin at 8:00 PM on Friday nights during the semester.

cards.title: Morning Walk in the Woods
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Nature
cards.notes: Explore the self-guiding nature trail around the ponds to spot turtles and local bird species in the Forest Preserve.
cards.short_summary: A 45-acre natural laboratory and woodland retreat located on the south side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zuck Arboretum features trails open to the public, including a self-guiding nature trail around the ponds.
cards.source_title: Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration at Drew
cards.access_notes: Trails are open to the public; enter through the gates near the baseball fields and lift the latch.

cards.title: Active Afternoon
cards.subtitle: Saturday Fitness Session
cards.notes: Use your student ID to access the fitness room, weight room, or the 200-meter indoor track for a workout.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic facility on campus, housing a pool, gym, and fitness centers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simon Forum facilities are open for the Drew community and require a valid Drew ID for entry.
cards.source_title: Simon Forum and Athletic Center | Drew University
cards.access_notes: Academic year hours: Mon-Fri 8am-10pm, Sat 10am-7pm, Sun 12pm-6pm.

cards.title: Explore the Rose City
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Out
cards.notes: Walk five minutes from campus to Main Street to browse local shops and grab a coffee or ice cream.
cards.short_summary: The historic and safe downtown area of Madison, NJ, located just steps from the university gates.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Madison is a five-minute walk from campus and features cafes, restaurants, and shops along Main Street.
cards.source_title: Discover Madison – Your Home Beyond the Forest
cards.access_notes: Easily accessible via the Lancaster Road entrance; most shops close by 6:00 PM or 8:00 PM.

cards.title: Find Your Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Prep
cards.notes: Scope out the silent study areas on the second floor or reserve a group study room for upcoming projects.
cards.short_summary: The main university library offering diverse study environments from social to silent.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose Memorial Library offers group study spaces, private day carrels, and designated silent study zones.
cards.source_title: Find Your Zone | Silent, Quiet, Social and Hybrid
cards.access_notes: Current Drew ID required for entry during late-night study hours.

cards.title: Visit the Historic Heart
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon History
cards.notes: Admire the Greek Revival architecture of Drew's original 1836 building, now serving as the administrative core.
cards.short_summary: A National Register of Historic Places mansion that is the symbolic center of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Hall is the original building on the Drew site, built in 1832-1836, and remains a focal point for the community.
cards.access_notes: Primarily houses offices; the exterior and main hall are accessible during business hours.

cards.title: Catch a Performance
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Culture
cards.notes: Check for student rush tickets or 'Under 35' discounts to see professional theatre right on campus.
cards.short_summary: An independent professional theatre company residency located on the Drew University campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey offers $35 tickets for those under 35 and student discounts for performances.
cards.access_notes: Box office opens 12:00 PM on performance days; check the seasonal calendar for showtimes.
